knowledge_used.how_applied: Copper-free ISO_BARRIER rule area on every layer between the HV classes and CTRL_SELV and between DRV_HS and DRV_LS; only reinforced-rated components bridge it.
Distances derived here from the standard for 440 V DC working voltage, PD2, material group IIIa; DESAT midpoint nets treated as full-bus nets in their own classes.
Ten KiCad net classes grouped by reference potential (CTRL_SELV, HV_VIN, HV_SW, HV_PGND, HV_VOUT, DRV_HS, DRV_LS, DESAT_HS, DESAT_LS, PE) with class-pair clearance rules.
1.0 mm non-plated slots under every barrier-crossing component whose land gap is below 9.0 mm; path arithmetic gap + 2 x board thickness shown.

Insulation-coordination review of each barrier part at 440 V DC reinforced: UCC21710-Q1, AMC1311, TMCS1133 pass on datasheet evidence; bias modules and relay coil-to-contact ratings surfaced as human-review items, not decided.
Protective-coordination expectation: DESAT/OC response < device SCWT; fuse shown analytically unable to protect the device (I^2t orders of magnitude apart) and assigned to wiring/board protection.
Hardware overcurrent path to the ePWM trip zone required; ADC-based protection not accepted as the primary path.
Rated insulating pads (>= 4 kV AC breakdown) on the shared PE-bonded heatsink; 5.0 mm / 3.0 mm from heatsink to HV copper and pins.
Rule gives the pattern (paralleled pours, stitched vias); the sizing method (IPC-2221 formula, via barrel area and resistance, vias per ampere) is added here with numbers for this converter.
Gate discharge resistors required so unpowered drivers cannot float gates during the start-up / shutdown sequence.
Hardware driver interlock listed as the last barrier in the interlock chain; dead time from the controller.
Principle 1 (isolation concept) and procedure step 2 (working voltage and insulation class at the node determine the driver rating) used to classify the barrier as reinforced at 440 V DC.
Principles 5-7 and procedure steps 1 and 5 (net classes, barrier keep-outs, slots) implemented; the skill explicitly leaves numeric distances to the standard, which this document supplies.
PCB constraint that the bias transformer/module straddles the barrier with slots is carried into the slot rule; the module rating itself is left to the bias-supply agent with a KR-SN-001 flag.
Rate-every-barrier-part step and divider-ladder creepage note used for the isolated amplifier / Hall sensor and HV divider placement.
Shared-sink insulation and creepage from a grounded sink to HV pins turned into the 5.0 mm heatsink rule and the PE-bonding requirement.
Not used for sizing; only the stored energy and discharge of whatever DC-link capacitance the capacitor agent selects is treated here, parametrically for 50-200 uF.

Decision 7 used only as a cross-check (8 mm creepage for 800 Vpk basic, three 1 mm slots, Tg >= 170 C); the 8 mm figure is not copied, the derived 9.0-10.0 mm reinforced rule is shown to be consistent with it.
Decision 6 class structure (PRIMARY, LOW-SIDE, HIGH-SIDE, DESAT-MIDPOINT, DRAIN) mirrored as KiCad classes; its 0.76 mm slot width noted; its distances were never extracted and are not reused.
Decision 9 (insulating pads on shared sinks) and decision 10 (bus copper repeated on three layers) used as patterns; TI's part choices and 800 V ratings not carried over.
Concerns gate-bias supply architecture and isolation capacitance, which belong to the bias-supply agent; no spacing or safety content.
Copper and via sizing rationale (widths, via plating assumption, loss) provided as the required evidence.
Control/power separation realised as the SELV domain behind the ISO_BARRIER keep-out.

markdown:
# Standards, insulation coordination, PCB spacing and safety basis (400 V -> 200 V, 5 kW SiC synchronous buck)

Verification tags used below: [V] = read from the text of EN 61800-5-1:2007 (Tables 3, 7, 9, 10; 4.3.6.2-4.3.6.5, 4.3.6.7, 4.3.11, 6.5.2), which reproduces the IEC 60664-1 Annex F tables (61800-5-1 Table 9 NOTE 3 states the derivation from IEC 60664-1 Table A.1); [S] = secondary source (manufacturer product page via search, distributor listing, application note); [U] = not verified. No value below is copied from a reference-design instance.

## 1. Scope, environment and classification

Non-isolated DC/DC power electronic converter system, 400 V DC in (360-440 V, 480 V/100 ms survival), 200 V DC / 25 A out, fed from a regulated DC bus or a current-limited laboratory supply; engineering prototype for a laboratory / industrial-cabinet environment: overvoltage category II, pollution degree 2, altitude <= 2000 m, FR4 with CTI 175-399 = material group IIIa (group definitions 61800-5-1 4.3.6.5.2 [V]: I >= 600, II 400-599, IIIa 175-399, IIIb 100-174).

Governing documents: IEC 62477-1 (PECS general safety; the working-voltage based method is identical to 61800-5-1, clause numbers [U]); IEC 61800-5-1:2007 used as the text-verified source of the numeric tables; IEC 60664-1 as the insulation-coordination basis; UL 840 as the harmonised North-American equivalent (cross-reference only, [U]); IPC-2221B Table 6-1 for functional conductor spacing [S]; IPC-2221/IPC-2152 for current capacity; IEC 62368-1 only as cross-reference (its 2 s discharge rule for pluggable equipment is not adopted, [S]).

Decisive voltage classes (61800-5-1 Table 3 [V]): DVC A <= 25 Vac rms / 35.4 Vpk / 60 V DC; DVC B <= 50 / 71 / 120 V DC; DVC C <= 1000 / 4500 / 1500 V DC. The 400 V bus, the 200 V output, the switch node, both gate-driver islands and the DESAT nets are DVC C; the 12 V auxiliary, DSP, JTAG, UART, user I/O and fan are DVC A. Accessible DVC A circuits need protective separation (double or reinforced insulation) from DVC C circuits (61800-5-1 4.3.3 / 4.3.4.2 [V]; SKILL-001 principle 1; KR-SN-001). Live parts of DVC C must sit behind an enclosure or barrier of at least IPXXB (4.3.3 [V]).

## 2. Insulation classes present and working voltages

Creepage is dimensioned with the r.m.s./DC working voltage, clearance and solid insulation with the recurring peak (4.3.6.2.1 NOTE 1 [V]); the 480 V / 100 ms event is a temporary overvoltage, not a working voltage.

| Pair | Class | Working voltage (creepage basis) | Recurring peak (clearance basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| VIN+ - PGND | functional | 440 V DC | 440 V (bus ringing), 480 V TOV |
| SW - PGND and SW - VIN+ | functional | Vin*sqrt(D) = 268-297 Vrms; designed as 440 V DC | 440 V + <= 20 % overshoot = 530 V (assumption A1) |
| VOUT+ - PGND | functional | 200 V DC, 220 V max (A2) | 220 V |
| VIN+ - VOUT+ | functional | 160-240 V DC, 280 V TOV | 280 V |
| SW - VOUT+ | functional | 179-219 Vrms | 240 V (280 V TOV) |
| Nets inside one driver island (gate, Kelvin source, VDD2/VSS2, DESAT node) vs its reference (SW or PGND) | functional | <= 25 V | <= 25 V |
| HS island vs VIN+ (HS drain); LS island vs SW (LS drain) | functional | 440 V DC in the off state | 530 V |
| DESAT midpoint nets vs every class except their own drain | functional | full bus, 440 V DC (KR-ISO-002) | 530 V |
| HS island vs LS island | functional | 440 V DC | 530 V |
| Any HV net vs PE / heatsink / chassis / mounting hardware | basic (class I) | 440 V DC (A4) | 530 V |
| Any HV net vs SELV control domain: isolated gate drivers, isolated amplifiers, Hall sensor, bias modules, digital isolators, relay coil-to-contact | reinforced (protective separation) | 440 V DC | 530 V |

## 3. Impulse withstand, clearance and creepage requirements

Impulse voltage (61800-5-1 Table 7 = IEC 60664-1 Table F.1 [V], interpolation not permitted): 300 V system -> OVC II 2500 V / OVC III 4000 V; 600 V system -> OVC II 4000 V / OVC III 6000 V. A 400 V DC bus rectified from 230/400 V TN mains is a 300 V system (4.3.6.2.1 NOTE 3 [V]); a transformer-isolated laboratory source at 400 V DC counts itself as a system voltage (NOTE 4 [V]) and falls in the 600 V row. The source is unspecified, so the design impulse is 4000 V for functional/basic insulation (covers OVC II at 600 V and OVC III at 300 V) and 6000 V for reinforced insulation (next higher step, 4.3.6.4.1 [V]).

Clearance (Table 9 = 60664-1 Table F.2, PD2, inhomogeneous field [V]): 2500 V -> 1.5 mm; 4000 V -> 3.0 mm; 6000 V -> 5.5 mm; 8000 V -> 8.0 mm; recurring-peak columns: 530 V -> 0.20 mm, 960 V -> 0.5 mm, 1600 V -> 1.5 mm, 2600 V -> 3.0 mm. Reinforced insulation also takes 1.6 x TOV and 2 x working peak (4.3.6.4.1 [V]): with TOV = 480 V and 2 x 530 V = 1060 V these give <= 1.6 mm, so 5.5 mm governs. If a reviewer treats the source as mains-connected (TOV 2550 V crest for the 600 V row, Table 7 [V]), 1.6 x TOV = 4080 V would interpolate to 6.4 mm: covered by the design rule below but flagged for review.

Creepage (Table 10 = 60664-1 Table F.4, interpolation permitted [V]; reinforced = 2 x basic; creepage never below the clearance, 4.3.6.5.1 [V]). PWB columns apply to printed boards and parts on them with comparable tolerance control, all material groups except IIIb (footnotes a, c [V]):

| Working voltage | PWB column, PD2 | Other insulators, PD2, IIIa |
|---|---|---|
| 200 V | 0.63 mm | 2.0 mm |
| 250 V | 1.0 mm | 2.5 mm |
| 320 V | 1.6 mm | 3.2 mm |
| 400 V | 2.0 mm | 4.0 mm |
| 440 V (interpolated) | 2.2 mm | 4.4 mm |
| 500 V | 2.5 mm | 5.0 mm |
| 630 V | 3.2 mm | 6.3 mm |

Derived requirements and the AIPE design rule (conservative: the "other insulators" IIIa column at 440 V interpolated, rounded up, never below clearance):

| Class | Clearance required | Creepage required (PWB / other insulators) | AIPE DRC value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reinforced HV - SELV | 5.5 mm (6 kV) | 5.0 -> 5.5 mm / 8.8-10.0 mm | 9.0 mm minimum copper gap on every layer, 10.0 mm target; slot wherever a land pattern gives < 9.0 mm |
| Basic HV - PE, heatsink, chassis | 3.0 mm (4 kV) | 2.5 -> 3.0 mm / 4.4-5.0 mm | 5.0 mm copper to earthed metal, PE pads and mounting holes; 3.0 mm absolute minimum |
| Functional HV - HV, 440 V class | 3.0 mm (4 kV; 4.3.6.3 transient-affected case [V]); 0.2 mm if designed to working voltage only | 2.5 -> 3.0 mm / 4.4-5.0 mm | 3.0 mm on outer layers (5.0 mm preferred), 1.0 mm on inner layers (solid insulation); component pin fields governed by the component |
| Functional 200-280 V class (VOUT+ pairs) | 3.0 mm if transient-affected | 1.0-1.6 mm / 2.5-3.2 mm | treated as the HV functional class: 3.0 mm outer, 1.0 mm inner |
| Functional <= 25 V inside a driver island | - | 0.04 mm | 0.3 mm |
| SELV control domain | - | - | 0.15-0.20 mm (fabrication minimum) |

IPC-2221B Table 6-1 [S] (functional spacing, peak voltage): 301-500 V: B1 internal 0.25 mm, B2 external uncoated 2.5 mm, B4 external permanent-polymer coated 0.8 mm; above 500 V add 0.0025 (B1) / 0.005 (B2) / 0.00305 (B4) mm per volt, giving 0.33 / 2.65 / 0.89 mm at 530 Vpk; 171-250 V: 0.2 / 1.25 / 0.4 mm. The IEC-derived 3.0 mm rule exceeds B2; solder mask is not credited as a B4 coating. Cross-check with the reference boards: CGD15SG00D2 uses 8 mm creepage for an 800 Vpk (566 Vrms) basic rating, where Table 10 (630 V row, IIIa) requires 6.3 mm, i.e. about 27 % margin (REF-WS-CGD15SG00D2 decision 7); the present 9.0-10.0 mm reinforced rule for 440 V DC sits consistently above that basic figure. The six spacing classes of CGD1700HB2M-UNA are mirrored in Section 4 (REF-WS-CGD1700HB2M-UNA decision 6; KR-ISO-003); its distances were never extracted and are not reused.

## 4. KiCad net classes, custom rules, slots

| Net class | Members | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| CTRL_SELV | DSP, 3V3/5V/12V, JTAG, UART, fan, relay coil, primary sides of all isolators and bias modules | SGND, bonded to PE |
| HV_VIN | VIN+, fuse and relay HV side, DC-link positive | PGND |
| HV_SW | SW, inductor input, HS power source, LS drain | PGND |
| HV_PGND | PGND, LS power source, DC-link and output negative | PGND |
| HV_VOUT | VOUT+, output capacitors positive | PGND |
| DRV_HS | HS gate, HS Kelvin source, HS VDD2/VSS2/COM, HS driver and bias secondaries | SW |
| DRV_LS | LS gate, LS Kelvin source, LS rails, LS driver and bias secondaries | PGND |
| DESAT_HS, DESAT_LS | nodes between the DESAT diodes and the driver | floating, full bus |
| PE | PE stud, heatsink, chassis, Y-capacitor PE side | earth |

Rules (KiCad clearance = copper gap; implement as custom rules conditioned on A.NetClass / B.NetClass, plus rule areas):
1. Any HV_*, DRV_*, DESAT_* vs CTRL_SELV: 9.0 mm on all layers; a 10 mm wide ISO_BARRIER keep-out (all copper layers) along the whole barrier; no copper crosses it (KR-ISO-001; SKILL-002 principle 5).
2. Any HV_*, DRV_*, DESAT_* vs PE: 5.0 mm (basic, strict column).
3. HV_VIN / HV_SW / HV_PGND / HV_VOUT all pairs; DRV_HS vs HV_VIN, HV_PGND, HV_VOUT, DRV_LS; DRV_LS vs HV_VIN, HV_SW, HV_VOUT; DESAT_HS/DESAT_LS vs every class except their own drain net: 3.0 mm on F.Cu/B.Cu, 1.0 mm on inner layers (KR-ISO-002, KR-ISO-003).
4. Same-reference pairs (DRV_HS vs HV_SW, DRV_LS vs HV_PGND, intra-class): 0.3 mm; CTRL_SELV intra-class 0.15-0.2 mm.
5. HV copper to board edge >= 1.0 mm, >= 5.0 mm where an earthed enclosure wall can touch the edge; HV copper to any mounting hole of the earthed heatsink >= 5.0 mm (SKILL-006 PCB constraints).
6. Slots (KR-ISO-004; SKILL-002 principle 7): under every barrier-crossing part whose primary-secondary land gap is below 9.0 mm (wide-body SOIC isolators have 7.6-8.0 mm land gaps against an 8 mm package rating; bias modules and transformers likewise): non-plated slot 1.0 mm wide (CGD15SG00D2 used three 1 mm slots, CGD1700HB2M-UNA 0.76 mm), extending >= 1 mm beyond the pad rows; surface path = gap + 2 x 1.6 mm board = 10.8-11.2 mm; check the path around the slot ends >= 9.0 mm. A slot between DRV_HS and DRV_LS is needed only if 3.0 mm cannot be held around the TO-247-4 pin field.
7. Component exception: inside the land pattern of a certified component (TO-247-4 at 2.54 mm pitch, DESAT diodes, isolator ICs) the component's own creepage governs; the rule applies to tracks and zones outside the land pattern. The DESAT diode bodies keep the full 3.0/5.0 mm distance to other groups (REF-WS-CGD1700HB2M-UNA decision 6).

## 5. DC-link discharge and labelling

61800-5-1:2007 4.3.11 [V]: capacitors shall be discharged to less than 60 V, or to a residual charge below 50 uC, within 5 s after removal of power; if not achievable, 6.5.2 [V] requires the warning symbol IEC 60417-5036 and an indication of the discharge time on the enclosure or near the capacitors, with the time stated in the manuals; connectors removable without a tool that expose conductors require 1 s or IPXXB protection. IEC 62477-1 carries the equivalent requirement (clause 4.4.9 in the current editions, wording [U]). Both the input bank (up to 480 V) and the output bank (200 V at no load) need discharge paths.

R_bleed <= t / (C * ln(V0 / 60 V)); P = V_op^2 / R:

| C | 5 s from 480 V | 60 s from 480 V | P at 440 V (60 s case) | stored energy at 480 V |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50 uF | <= 48 kOhm, 4.0 W | <= 577 kOhm | 0.34 W | 5.8 J |
| 100 uF | <= 24 kOhm, 8.1 W | <= 288 kOhm | 0.67 W | 11.5 J |
| 200 uF | <= 12 kOhm, 16 W | <= 144 kOhm | 1.34 W | 23 J |

Output bank: 200 uF from 220 V in 60 s -> <= 231 kOhm, 0.17 W. A passive 5 s bleed costs 4-16 W, so the recommended prototype scheme is passive bleeders for <= 60 s plus the 60417-5036 label with "60 s" and one LED discharge indicator per bank, with an optional active discharge (relay-switched resistor or converter-controlled dump) if 5 s is wanted. Bleeders are two series resistors each seeing <= 240 V (Vishay PR02, 2 W, 500 V element rating [S]). Terminals are screw or ring-lug types under IPXXB covers so the 1 s rule does not apply. Labels: IEC 60417-5036 + discharge time, ISO 7010 W012, PE symbol IEC 60417-5019 at the stud, hot-surface IEC 60417-5041 at the heatsink, rating plate (400 V DC in, 200 V DC / 25 A out, 5 kW, 50 kHz, DVC C, "480 V DC max", "AI-generated engineering prototype - human review required").

## 6. Accessible interfaces, earthing, Y-capacitors

JTAG, UART, user I/O, 12 V auxiliary and fan are DVC A with protective separation from all DVC C circuits; the control ground is bonded to PE at one point (PELV), which makes PC-connected debuggers safe and removes the "earthed DVC A outside an equipotential zone" case of 4.3.4.2 [V]. The external 12 V supply must itself be a safety-isolated SELV/PELV source (reinforced from mains, limited power); its connector is SELV-only and must not be routable to any HV net. Every barrier crosser is reinforced-rated for >= 440 V DC working voltage (KR-SN-001): UCC21710-Q1 (5.7 kVrms, 1.5 kVrms working, > 8 mm) and AMC1311 (7 kVpk, 1500 Vrms working) satisfy it with datasheet evidence; TMCS1133 (950 Vrms / 1343 V DC reinforced working, >= 8 mm) satisfies it; the per-channel bias modules (RECOM R12P2 series: 6.4 kVDC isolation, reinforced working-voltage rating not found) and the input relay coil-to-contact insulation are human-review items. Heatsink and chassis are PE-bonded class I parts; both TO-247-4 devices sit on rated insulating pads (KR-TH-002; TIDA-010054 decision 9 pattern) with breakdown >= 4 kV AC, and the heatsink body keeps 5.0 mm / 3.0 mm (creepage / clearance) from all HV copper and pins. PGND is not hard-bonded to PE because the source earthing is unknown; a configurable link, a high-impedance reference (2 x 1 MOhm, 500 V-rated) and optional Y2 capacitors (<= 10 nF per rail, 300 Vac Y2 with DC rating >= 1 kV [S]) are provided. With DC supply the Y-capacitor current is only switching ripple: 10 nF with 2 Vpp at 50 kHz gives 1.8 mA unweighted, below the customary 3.5 mA touch-current limit [U]; the capacitors bridge HV to PE (basic), so Y2 is sufficient and Y1 is not needed.

## 7. Safe start-up / shutdown, test interface, protective coordination

Sequence: 12 V aux on -> DSP boot with PWM pins forced low -> driver UVLO/RDY good -> input relay or precharge closes (inrush into the DC link from a stiff bus must be limited by precharge or by the laboratory supply's current limit, A7) -> bus within UVLO window (340 V start / 320 V stop) -> soft-start duty ramp -> run. Shutdown: PWM off, relay open, discharge, LED indicators dark before any contact. Interlocks: gate-driver FAULT/RDY wired to the ePWM trip zone, OVP 460 V and overcurrent comparators to the trip zone, over-temperature and fan-tach to the trip zone or a slow shutdown, an SELV emergency-stop/enable input, hardware driver interlock as last barrier (KR-GD-009), gate-source discharge resistors so an unpowered driver cannot float the gate (KR-GD-007). Test interface: HV probing only with isolated differential probes rated >= 1000 V CAT II; HV test points as recessed 4 mm safety sockets or probe loops >= 9.0 mm from any SELV copper; V_GS points at the device side of R_G (SKILL-002 procedure 8) are for isolated probes only; oscilloscope grounds only on the SELV side. Protective coordination (KR-PR-001, KR-SN-005): the DESAT/overcurrent path (blanking + detection + soft turn-off) must be shorter than the selected device's short-circuit withstand time, typically a few microseconds for 1200 V SiC (device-specific, from the datasheet); the DSP trip zone acts within a switching period; firmware limits act over milliseconds; the input fuse acts last. A fuse cannot protect the MOSFET: a 200 A / 2 us event is 0.08 A^2s, orders of magnitude below any 20 A fuse melting I^2t (KLKD020 value not found); the fuse protects wiring, board copper and capacitors. Input fuse: I_in = 5000 / (360 x 0.98) = 14.2 A, 15.6 A at 110 % overload; Littelfuse KLKD020 (20 A, 600 Vac/dc, fast-acting, 100 kA AC and 10 kA DC per UL 248-19 or 50 kA DC per UL 248-14 [S]) gives 20 x 0.8 = 16 A continuous application (0.8 factor A8) and a DC interrupting rating above any laboratory or DC-bus prospective current.

## 8. PCB manufacturing constraints and copper sizing

Standard pooled 70 um (2 oz) fabrication (capabilities [S], confirm with the fabricator): minimum track/space 0.20 mm on 2 oz outer layers, 0.25 mm recommended for yield; solder-mask dam >= 0.15 mm at 2 oz (0.10 mm is a typical absolute minimum), mask expansion 0.05 mm; minimum drill 0.3 mm (seed), annular ring >= 0.20 mm at 2 oz; plated slots >= 0.5-0.6 mm wide, non-plated routed slots >= 0.8-1.0 mm; via plating 25 um nominal (IPC-6012 class 2 average >= 20 um); 1.6 mm board (2.0 mm acceptable for a 4-layer 2 oz stack); copper-to-edge >= 0.5 mm (HV: see Section 4).

Current capacity, IPC-2221 formula I = k * dT^0.44 * A^0.725 (A in mil^2, k = 0.048 external / 0.024 internal [S]), dT = 20 K, 70 um copper: 25 A -> 0.585 mm^2 = 8.4 mm external, 1.52 mm^2 = 21.7 mm internal; 12.5 A -> 0.225 mm^2 = 3.2 mm external, 0.585 mm^2 = 8.4 mm internal; 27.5 A (10 s overload) -> 9.5 mm external, with a steady-state rise of (27.5/25)^2 x 20 = 24 K that the 10 s event does not reach. IPC-2152 chart values were not obtained [U]; IPC-2152 shows the IPC-2221 internal derating to be overly pessimistic, so the IPC-2221 widths are a conservative basis. Design: VIN+, PGND, SW and VOUT+ carried as >= 10 mm wide pours on the outer layers and repeated on inner layers so that each inner pour carries <= 12.5 A (>= 8.4 mm), paralleled with via arrays (KR-PCB-006; PE-PCB-006; TIDA-010054 decision 10 pattern). Via method: 0.5 mm finished hole with 25 um plating -> barrel area pi x (0.5 + 0.025) x 0.025 = 0.0412 mm^2 (64 mil^2, equivalent to a 0.59 mm wide 70 um trace), R = 1.72e-8 x 1.6e-3 / 4.12e-8 = 0.67 mOhm per via, 1.8 A per via with the internal constant (3.7 A external); 25 A -> 14 vias, 21 with a 1.5x margin (e.g. 3 x 7 at 1.0 mm pitch, 0.032 mOhm, 0.02 W); 0.3 mm vias carry 1.3 A each. DRC proxy: >= 1 via per 1.5 A of layer-transfer current.

Secondary-source or unverified: IPC-2221B Table 6-1 values; IPC-2152 chart values (not obtained); IEC 62477-1 clause numbers and wording; UL 840 and IEC 62368-1 cross-references; 3.5 mA touch-current limit; fabricator capability figures; KLKD020 datasheet (I^2t not found), PR02 element voltage, TDK B32021 DC rating, Sil-Pad 2000 breakdown (search-snippet level).
